subject: ENGR
title: Introduction to Ohio State and Engineering
description: Introduction to the University community and College of Engineering: Strategies for successful transition, academic requirements, University procedures, grading system, resources, overview of engineering academic areas of study and services.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: Enrollment in the College of Engineering. Not open to students with credit for FAES 1100, ArtsCol 1100, ArtsSci 1100, HumanEc 1100, and Exp 1100.

matches.match_rationale: A 1-credit introduction to the university and the College of Engineering; it creates the first-year orientation concept.

subject: ENGR
title: Fundamentals of Engineering I
description: Engineering problem solving utilizing computational tools such as Excel and MATLAB; hands-on experimentation; modeling; teamwork; written, oral and visual communications.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq or concur: Math 1140, or 1141; or Math 1150 or above. Not open to students with credit for Engr 1182.01, 1182.02, 1182.03, 1182.04, 1282.01H, 1282.02H, 1282.03H, 1282.04H, 1186.01, 1187, or 1188.

matches.match_rationale: First half of OSU's first-year engineering sequence: computational tools (Excel, MATLAB), experiments, teamwork, and communication.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus I
description: Differential and integral calculus of one real variable.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 1148 and 1149, or in 1144, 1150, or 150, or Math Placement Level L. Not open to students with credit for 1152 or 152.xx, or above.

matches.match_rationale: Differential and integral calculus of one variable.

subject: PHYSICS
title: Mechanics, Work and Energy, Thermal Physics
description: Calculus-based introduction to classical physics: Newton's laws, work and energy, fluids, thermodynamics; for students in physical sciences, mathematics, and engineering.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: A required calculus-based mechanics course with lab; OSU names the science instead of offering a choice, and lab-science covers a program that requires one specific science.
matches.notes: Course row mapped to a slot concept (allowed for lab-science only; decided in step 10).

subject: CSE
title: Introduction to Computer Programming in Java
description: Introduction to computer programming and to problem solving techniques using computer programs; programming lab experience.
notes: Not part of the 126-hour requirements: students take it unless they place out of it (CSE 2221's prerequisite), so counts_toward_total = false.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: Math 1120, 1130, 1140, 1148, 1149, 1150, or 1151, or Math Placement Level M.

matches.match_rationale: A first programming course (in Java) for students who don't place out of it.

subject: CSE
title: Software I: Software Components
description: Intellectual foundations of software engineering; design-by-contract principles; mathematical modeling of software functionality; component-based software from client perspective; layered data representation.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: 1212, 1221, 1222, 1223, 1224, Engr 1221, 1281.01H, 1281.02H, or CSE Placement Level A. Prereq or concur: Math 1151, 1161.01, or 1161.02. Not open to students with credit for 5022.

matches.match_rationale: OSU's second programming course (Software I): component-based design and design-by-contract in Java; no UC course matches it, so it creates the Programming II concept.

subject: ENGR
title: Fundamentals of Engineering II
description: Introduction to 3D visualization and CAD; engineering design-build process; teamwork; written, oral and visual communications; project management.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: 1181.01, or 1181.02, or 1281.01H, or 1281.02H, or 1281.03H. Prereq or Concur: Math 1141; or Math 1151 or above. Not open to students with credit for 1186.01, or 1187, or 1188; not repeatable if credit earned for 1182.01, or 1182.02, or 1182.03, or 1182.04, or 1282.01H, or 1282.02H, or 1282.03H, or 1282.04H.

matches.match_rationale: Second half of OSU's first-year engineering sequence: 3D visualization, CAD, and a design-build project.

subject: MATH
title: Engineering Mathematics A
description: Techniques of integration, Taylor series, differential calculus of several variables. Applications.
notes: Corrected from the sample schedule: Schedule prints 'MATH 1152 | 3'; the requirements list says Math 1151, 1172 (10 hours), MATH 1172 is 5 credits, and the term total (15) only adds up with 5. Corrected to MATH 1172, 5 cr.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 1114 (114), 1151, 1156, 1161.xx, 152.xx, 161.xx, or 161.01H. Not open to students with credit for 1152, 1534 (153.xx), or 1544 (154), or for any Math class numbered 1172 or above, or for any quarter-system Math class numbered 254.xx or above. Not open to students majoring in Math, pre-Actuarial Science, or Actuarial Science.

matches.match_rationale: Covers techniques of integration and Taylor series like Calculus II, but adds multivariable differential calculus.

title: GE Foundations: Writing and Information Literacy
description: A first-year writing course that teaches academic writing, argument, revision, and finding and evaluating sources. Students write several papers for different audiences and purposes. Many universities require one such course of all students.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: A gen-ed category slot; its content is first-year composition, but as a choice from a list it maps to the gen-ed slot.

subject: GENED
title: GE Launch Seminar
description: This course is first GE Bookend class. The Launch seminar provides a strong introduction for the broad goals of the General Education program, introduces key skills, and supports sustained growth in terms of attaining program goals. This course is graded S/U.
notes: GE Launch Seminar.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: A 1-credit first-year seminar that introduces the General Education program; a university orientation course rather than CS content.

subject: CSE
title: Software II: Software Development and Design
description: Data representation using hashing, search trees, and linked data structures; algorithms for sorting; using trees for language processing; component interface design; best practices in Java.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: 2221 with a C- or above. Concur: 2321. Not open to students with credit for 2231.01.

matches.match_rationale: Hashing, search trees, linked data structures, and sorting, implemented in Java.

subject: CSE
title: Foundations I: Discrete Structures
description: Propositional and first-order logic; basic proof techniques; graphs, trees; analysis of algorithms; asymptotic analysis; recurrence relations.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: 2122, 2123, 2124 or 2221; and Math 1151 or 1161. Concur (for students with credit for 2221): 2231.

matches.match_rationale: Logic, proof techniques, graphs and trees, and asymptotic analysis for computing.

subject: STAT
title: Introduction to Probability and Statistics for Engineers
description: Introduction to probability, Bayes theorem; discrete and continuous random variables, expected value, probability distributions; point and interval estimation; hypotheses tests for means and proportions; least squares regression.
notes: Corrected from the sample schedule: Schedule prints 4 hours; the requirements list and the course itself are 3. Corrected to 3 cr.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: Math 1152, 1161.xx, 1172, 1181H, or equiv, or permission of instructor. Not open to students with credit for 3440, 3450, 3450.01, 3450.02, 3460, 3470, or 3470.02.

matches.match_rationale: Calculus-based probability and statistics for engineers, including estimation, tests, and regression.

title: Math or Science Elective
description: An additional mathematics or natural science course chosen from a list approved by the program. Typical choices include further calculus or differential equations, a second physics course, chemistry, or biology.
notes: OSU: 8 hours of science/math electives from an approved list (see Buckeye Degree Planner).
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: An 8-hour choice of math or science courses from an approved list; neither lab-science nor technical-elective fits, so it creates the concept.

title: GE Foundations: Social and Behavioral Sciences
description: A general education course on how individuals, groups, and societies behave, from a field such as psychology, sociology, economics, or political science. These courses introduce the field's research methods and main theories.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: A gen-ed category slot chosen from an approved list.

subject: CSE
title: Foundations II: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Design/analysis of algorithms and data structures; divide-and-conquer; sorting and selection, search trees, hashing, graph algorithms, string matching; probabilistic analysis; randomized algorithms; NP-completeness.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: 2122, 2123, 2124 or 2231; and 2321; and Stat 3460, 3470 or 3201; and enrollment in CSE, CIS, ECE, Data Analytics, Math majors or CS minor. Not open to students with credit for 5331.

matches.match_rationale: Design and analysis of algorithms (divide and conquer, graph algorithms, randomized algorithms, NP-completeness); partial because it also covers data structures (search trees, hashing).
Its rationale already notes it covers data structures (search trees, hashing) alongside algorithms.

subject: CSE
title: Systems I: Introduction to Low-Level Programming and Computer Organization
description: Introduction to computer architecture at machine and assembly language level; pointers and addressing; C programming at machine level; computer organization.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: 2122, 2123, or 2231; and 2321 or Math 2566; and enrollment in CSE, CIS, Data Analytics, Music (BS), Eng Physics, or Math major.

matches.match_rationale: Machine-level programming in C and assembly, pointers, and computer organization.

subject: MATH
title: Foundations of Higher Mathematics
description: Introduction to logic, proof techniques, set theory, number theory, real numbers.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: Major or minor in Math, CSE, CIS, ECE, IMME, STAT, STEMED-PRE or STEMED-BS, and: If Math, IMME, STAT, STEMED-PRE or STEMED-BS: Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 2153, 2162.xx, 2173, or 2182H. If CIS, CSE or ECE: Prereq: A grade of C- or above in CSE 2321; and a grade of C- or above in 1161.xx, 1172, 1181H, 1534, 1544, 1152, or 4181H.

matches.match_rationale: A mathematics proofs course (logic, proof techniques, sets, number theory); different enough from discrete-math to create its own concept.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Digital Logic
description: Introduction to the theory and practice of combinational and clocked sequential networks.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: Math 1148 or 1151. Not open to students with credit for 2000, 2000.02, 2000.07, 2001, 2010, or 2017.

matches.match_rationale: Combinational and clocked sequential networks; no UC course covers digital logic, so it creates the concept.

title: GE Foundations: Race, Ethnicity and Gender Diversity
description: A general education course on how race, ethnicity, and gender shape people's experiences and social structures, often with a focus on the United States. Courses come from fields such as history, sociology, and ethnic or gender studies.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: A gen-ed category slot chosen from an approved list.

subject: CSE
title: Systems II: Introduction to Operating Systems
description: Introduction to operating system concepts: process, CPU scheduling, memory management, file system and storage, and multi-threaded programming.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: 2421, or 2451 and ECE 2560; and enrollment in CSE, CIS, Data Analytics, Engr Physics, or ECE major. Not open to students with credit for 5431.

matches.match_rationale: Processes, CPU scheduling, memory management, file systems, and multithreaded programming.

subject: CSE
title: CSE 390X (CSE 3901 or CSE 3902 or CSE 3903)
description: A team software project course in which students design, build, and document a sizable system. Students choose the kind of system: web applications, interactive systems such as games, or system software. These courses emphasize teamwork, design, testing, and written documentation.
notes: Student chooses one: CSE 3901 Project: Design, Development, and Documentation of Web Applications | CSE 3902 Project: Design, Development, and Documentation of Interactive Systems | CSE 3903 Project: Design, Development, and Documentation of System Software.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: All three options are team project courses (web, interactive, or system software) with design and documentation; creates the project-course concept.

subject: ECE
title: Electronics for CSE majors
description: Electronics course for CSE majors. Circuit analysis and design around embedded systems.
notes: Corrected from the sample schedule: Schedule prints ECE 2060 a second time (it is already in Year 2 Spring); the requirements list has ECE 2360 (Electronics for CSE Majors), which is otherwise missing. Corrected to ECE 2360.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: Engr 1182.01, 1182.02, 1182.03, 1282.01H, 1282.02H, 1282.03H, or 1282.04H, or 1186 and 1187 and 1188 concurrent; and Math 1152, 1161.01, 1161.02, 1172, or 1181H; and Physics 1250 or 1260; and CPHR 2.00 or above; and enrollment in CSE major. Not open to students with credit for 2020 or 2300.

matches.match_rationale: Circuit analysis and design around embedded systems; creates the electronics concept.

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra
description: Matrix algebra, vector spaces and linear maps, bases and dimension, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, applications.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: A grade of C- or above in 1172, 1544, 2153, 2162.xx, 2182H, or 4182H; or a grade of C- or above in both 1152 and CSE 2321. Not open to students with credit for 4568 or 5520H.

matches.match_rationale: Matrix algebra, vector spaces, linear maps, eigenvalues.

title: GE Foundations: Historical and Cultural Studies
description: A general education course that studies a past period, culture, or society through historical sources and methods. These courses help students explain how the past shapes the present and interpret historical evidence.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: A gen-ed category slot chosen from an approved list.

subject: CSE
title: CSE 32X1 (CSE 3231 or CSE 3241)
description: A choice between a software engineering course (requirements, design, testing, project management, and team process) and a database course (the relational model, SQL, database design, and query processing).
notes: Student chooses one: CSE 3231 Software Engineering Techniques | CSE 3241 Introduction to Database Systems.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: Option CSE 3231: software lifecycle, requirements, architecture, design, testing, and project management.
Option CSE 3241: database design, the ER model, normalization, SQL, and relational algebra.

subject: CSE
title: CSE 34X1 (CSE 3421 or CSE 3461)
description: A choice between a computer architecture course (instruction sets, processor design, pipelining, and memory hierarchy) and a computer networking course (network layers, the Internet protocols, routing, and network applications).
notes: Student chooses one: CSE 3421 Introduction to Computer Architecture | CSE 3461 Computer Networking and Internet Technologies.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: Option CSE 3421: computer architecture (instruction sets, pipelining, memory subsystems); partial because it assumes the machine-level programming of CSE 2421.
Option CSE 3461: network protocols, TCP/IP, wireless, and network security.

subject: CSE
title: CSE 35X1 (CSE 3521 or CSE 3541)
description: A choice between an introductory artificial intelligence course (search, knowledge representation, reasoning, and basic machine learning) and an introductory computer graphics or game and animation course (rendering, transformations, and interactive animation).
notes: Student chooses one: CSE 3521 Survey of Artificial Intelligence I: Basic Techniques | CSE 3541 Computer Game and Animation Techniques.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: Option CSE 3521: a survey of AI: problem solving, knowledge representation, and machine learning.
Option CSE 3541: algorithms and mathematics of computer animation and video games; no existing concept covers graphics, so it creates one.

title: Math or Science Elective
description: An additional mathematics or natural science course chosen from a list approved by the program. Typical choices include further calculus or differential equations, a second physics course, chemistry, or biology.
notes: OSU: 8 hours of science/math electives from an approved list (see Buckeye Degree Planner).
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: An 8-hour choice of math or science courses from an approved list; neither lab-science nor technical-elective fits, so it creates the concept.

subject: CSE
title: Social, Ethical, and Professional Issues in Computing
description: Social, ethical, and professional issues facing computing professionals; ethical principles; discussion of case studies.
notes: Ethics requirement: the sheet allows CSE 2501 (1 hr) plus a separate 4-hour GE Theme, or PHILOS 2338 (4 hr), which also counts as the Citizenship Theme, plus a 1-hour free elective. The CSE 2501 path is used here (decided with the user).
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: 2122, 2123, or 2231; and GE writing and comm course: level 2, or GE foundation writing and info literacy course; and enrollment in CSE or CIS or DA major, or Information Security minor; or Grad standing. Not open to students with credit for 5501.

matches.match_rationale: Social, ethical, and professional issues in computing through case studies; creates the computing-ethics concept.

title: GE Theme
description: An upper-level general education course in an interdisciplinary theme, such as citizenship, sustainability, or health and well-being. Theme courses ask students to connect ideas across fields and apply them to a broad question.
notes: OSU requires two GE Themes of 4 hours each: Citizenship for a Diverse and Just World, and a Theme of the student's choice. The schedule doesn't say which goes where. PHILOS 2338 can also count as the Citizenship Theme (see CSE 2501). This one is not needed if PHILOS 2338 is taken.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: Two 4-hour upper-level gen-ed Theme slots chosen from approved lists.

subject: CSE
title: Principles of Programming Languages
description: Formal languages and grammars; recursive descent parsing; data types, expressions, control structures, parameter passing; compilers and interpreters; memory management; functional programming principles.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option
prerequisites: Prereq: 2231, 2331 (680), and 2421, and 3901 (560), 3902, or 3903. Not open to students with credit for 5341 (655).

matches.match_rationale: Grammars and parsing, language features, compilers and interpreters, and functional programming.

title: Technical Elective
description: An advanced computer science course chosen by the student, sometimes with a limited number of approved courses from related fields. Common options cover areas such as machine learning, security, graphics, networking, and software engineering. Technical electives let students go deeper in an area of interest.
notes: OSU: 17 hours; at least 9 in CSE courses at the 3000 level or higher, at most 8 in approved non-CSE courses at the 2000 level or higher. In the Individualized option, chosen with an advisor.
plan: CSE curriculum sheet with sample schedule, July 2025 (effective AU24), Individualized option

matches.match_rationale: Mostly upper-level CSE courses (at least 9 of 17 hours), with up to 8 hours of approved non-CSE courses.
